overview: The Parthian Empire was a major Iranian state that rivaled Rome for control of the Near East for nearly five centuries. Known for mounted archers and feudal administration, it facilitated Silk Road trade and maintained Iranian cultural identity.

items.text: The Parthian shot: mounted archers could fire accurately backwards while retreating at full gallop.
Heavy cataphract cavalry with armored horses and riders shocked enemy formations.
Controlled Silk Road routes between Rome and China, profiting enormously from transit trade.
Diplomatic contacts recorded with Han China, including an envoy received in 97 CE.
Zoroastrianism practiced alongside Greek, Mesopotamian and local religions in a tolerant framework.
The Arsacid dynasty claimed descent from the Achaemenids to legitimize their rule.
Parthian administrative practices and feudal structures influenced the Sasanian Empire.
Iranian cultural identity maintained through nearly five centuries of foreign pressures.

fall.text: Ardashir I defeated the last Parthian king Artabanus IV and established the Sasanian dynasty.
